newsitem.title: USA: Employee health care costs up 3 pct in 1997 - report.
newsitem.headline: Employee health care costs up 3 pct in 1997 - report.

text.p: Health care costs of active employees will grow three percent in 1997 for large employers, compared with four percent in 1996, according to a survey by consulting firm Towers Perrin.

The management consulting company's 1997 Health Care Cost Survey also found that health covereage for retirees under age 65 will increase four percent, but costs for Medicare-eligible retiress, who are age 65 and older, will rise seven percent.
Last year, retiree medical coverage costs rose four percent for those under 65 and three percent for for those over 65, the company said.
"It is noteworthy that the cost increase for retirees age 65 and older is more than double the increase of last year," said William Falk, a pricipal of Towers Perrin in a press release.

"However, this continuing overall moderate growth appears to reflect the ongoing shift toward managed health care delivery systems, intensifying competition between health plans in many local health care marketplaces and the low general inflation rate," he said.
The Towers Perrin study surveys 148 large organizations, primarily Fortune 1000 companies, that provide data on the cost of insured and self-insured medical and dental plans for the coming year.
